statements.proposition: This change refactors vllm env handling to type-introspected parsing while maintaining 100% backwards compatibility.
statements.label: FALSE
statements.note: Refactor itself happened (vllm/envs.py removed, vllm/envs/ package added), but the 100% backwards-compatibility part is contradicted by a concrete removed public name still used elsewhere: module-level dict `environment_variables`. Also the PR text itself says path variables changed from str to pathlib.Path.
evidence: file list: vllm/envs.py removed (-1272); vllm/envs/__init__.py added (+296); vllm/envs/_variables.py added (+341); only 3 files changed

base vllm/envs.py line 229 defines `environment_variables: dict[str, Callable]`; head vllm/envs/__init__.py and _variables.py contain no definition of `environment_variables` (grep, only `environment_variables_to_hash`)
vllm/ray/ray_env.py at head SHA 0b85cc9 line 57: `for v in set(envs.environment_variables)...`, unchanged by the PR; head __getattr__ raises AttributeError for names not in __defaults, so this breaks
PR message: 'cache_root = envs.VLLM_CACHE_ROOT  # Returns pathlib.Path (was string)'

statements.proposition: After this change, the Path-valued env variables (e.g. VLLM_CACHE_ROOT) work seamlessly wherever the former string values were used.
statements.label: CANNOT_TELL
statements.note: Path is not a str, so string operations would break, but the concrete uses I found at head (os.path.join(envs.VLLM_CACHE_ROOT, ...) in vllm/compilation/backends.py:527 and all_reduce_utils.py:233) accept Path. I did not audit every use, so no concrete break was settled. It is also an example comment rather than a precise statement.
evidence: vllm/compilation/backends.py line 527 and vllm/distributed/device_communicators/all_reduce_utils.py line 233 pass envs.VLLM_CACHE_ROOT as an argument (join-style use)
